search_log: Searched "Executive Orders" "Tom Clancy" excerpt, first chapter, and read sample; opened Penguin Random House, Hachette UK, Google Books, and Open Library records.
Publisher sample controls and Google Books/Open Library previews did not expose sustained searchable prose, so their catalog descriptions were not treated as person evidence.
Searched "Executive Orders" third-person, omniscient, point of view, narrator, and narrative perspective; opened the eNotes structural analysis and SoBrief's explicit POV analysis.
Opened the official Tom Clancy product page and the contemporary Washington Post review to distinguish Ryan's embedded first-person thought from the book's third-person narration.
A non-authorized full-text result was discovered during excerpt searching but was not relied upon because stronger attributable sources were available.
person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and third-person, moving among Jack Ryan and many other characters while sometimes entering their thoughts. The clearest quote evidence is q00112 and the narratorial framing in q00118-q00119; most shorter event quotations are conservatively unmarked because a name or he alone cannot diagnose narrator person. First-person language in q00084, the speeches, and the official product-page teaser belongs to character speech or direct thought, while second-person instances are dialogue or universal maxims. Whole-book structural analysis and an explicit POV source agree with an interior passage reproduced by a contemporary review. No credible evidence indicates sustained first- or second-person base sections; the only material uncertainty is that accessible authorized sample prose was limited.
